title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
content: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.
